text:
jordan_support: Hey team, customer (acct 8832) on Private/VPC deployment reports intermittent TLS handshake failures to our inference endpoint. Happens ~every 5-10 minutes for a few minutes, then clears. They said this started after they applied a perimeter FW firmware update. Error seen on client side: 'ECONNRESET during SSL handshake' and a lot of SYN retries.
lee_neteng: Can you paste a short repro and any captures? Need traceroute/tcpdump + sample curl/openssl output. Also which AZ/region for their private nodes?
jordan_support: Repro steps from customer:
- from their app host: `curl -v --resolve model.private.redwood:443:10.10.50.12 https://model.private.redwood:443/health`
- sometimes it fails with: `* SSL_connect: SSL_ERROR_SYSCALL in connection to model.private.redwood:443` then `Connection reset by peer`
They attached a short tcpdump. Region: us-west-2, private subnet.
maya_sre: Paste the relevant tcpdump lines (no full pcap needed). Also include `sudo conntrack -L | tail -n 20` and `sudo iptables -t mangle -S` if possible.
jordan_support: tcpdump excerpt from their host (anonymized IPs):
```
12:02:14.123456 IP (tos 0xb8, ttl 64, id 54321, offset 0, flags [DF]) 10.10.50.12.54321 > 52.12.34.56.443: Flags [S], seq 0x1a2b3c4d, win 64240, options [mss 1460,sackOK,TS val 123456 ecr 0,nop,wscale 7], length 0
12:02:14.223789 IP (tos 0x00, ttl 63) 52.12.34.56.443 > 10.10.50.12.54321: RST, seq 0x0, win 0, length 0
12:02:19.987654 IP (tos 0xb8) 10.10.50.12.54322 > 52.12.34.56.443: Flags [S], seq 0x9f8e7d6c, length 0
12:02:20.088001 IP (tos 0x00) 52.12.34.56.443 > 10.10.50.12.54322: Flags [S.], seq 0x0, ack 0x9f8e7d6d, win 65535, length 0
```
Note the alternating TOS/DSCP: first SYN shows `tos 0xb8` (DSCP=46 / EF), then reply comes back with tos 0x00 and sometimes a RST.
lee_neteng: Interesting — DSCP=46 (0xb8) is EF/high-priority marking. Some legacy/enterprise perimeter devices will rate-limit or drop EF traffic or treat it differently, even when forwarding to NATs. Can you also get a short flow log from their perimeter FW for the same timestamps?
toni_infra: We pulled logs from their on-prem firewall (they gave us an extract). Log entries around 12:02:14 show repeated `policy: drop - DSCP match - exceed-rate` for traffic sourced from 10.10.50.12 -> 52.12.34.56:443. So their FW is configured to throttle EF-marked packets to enforce QoS, and the SYNs that carry EF are being dropped intermittently.
maya_sre: That explains the handshake resets. TCP SYNs are dropped, client retries with new ephemeral port or lower rate, sometimes succeeding when SYNs not marked EF or when they hit a different microwindow.
jordan_support: Customer says they didn't explicitly set DSCP but their application lib sets traffic to EF to prioritize ML inference. They rolled out a new FW update that tightened enforcement, so previously the SYNs passed.
lee_neteng: Short-term mitigation options:
- Ask customer to clear DSCP for traffic to our inference endpoints (map to CS0) on their app hosts or egress NAT
- Or add a transient rule on their perimeter FW to allow EF for destination 52.12.34.56/32:443
- On our side, we can recommend route/loadbalancer adjustments but we shouldn't change our endpoint behaviour. Best to neutralize DSCP at customer boundary.
toni_infra: We suggested a quick mangle rule they can apply on their host (Linux):
```
# clear DSCP/TOS for outbound to inference endpoints
sudo iptables -t mangle -A OUTPUT -p tcp --dport 443 -d 52.12.34.56 -j TOS --set-tos 0x00
```
They applied it to their egress NAT host and re-ran the repro.
jordan_support: After applying the iptables rule, customer reports 30+ successful handshakes with no ECONNRESET. They also confirmed their perimeter FW logs no longer show the DSCP drop entries.
maya_sre: Can we get the customer to run this verify command and paste output? `openssl s_client -connect 52.12.34.56:443 -servername model.private.redwood -msg` — that prints handshake messages, good for validation.
jordan_support: Customer ran it, attached trimmed output: handshake completes and returns server cert. So resolved for now.
lee_neteng: Action items:
- jordan_support: document this case in KB: "DSCP/EF markings causing perimeter FW drop -> TLS handshake resets to private endpoints" with repro and mitigation steps.
- maya_sre: recommend adding a note to Private deployment quickstart that customers should normalize DSCP/TOS for outbound inference calls (or whitelist EF for endpoints).
- toni_infra: follow up with customer to see if they'll change app lib to not mark EF for TLS port or maintain NAT mangle permanently.
toni_infra: Customer will prefer host-level TOS clearing on their egress NAT as a permanent fix. They also scheduled a FW policy change but want to keep mangle for immediate safety.
deploy-bot: CI alert: KB doc created (kb/8832-dscp-inference-handshake) :white_check_mark:
maya_sre: Great. Also leave a note for Support runbook: when you see `tos 0xb8` on SYN and intermittent RSTs/handshake resets, check perimeter QoS/DSCP policing before chasing conntrack or NAT issues.
jordan_support: Thanks all. I'll close the support ticket once customer confirms no recurrence after 24h. :thumbsup:
monitor-bot: Incident follow-up scheduled in 24h for acct 8832.
jordan_support: Closing note: fixed via host mangle rule; root cause = perimeter FW introduced stricter DSCP policing in recent firmware update that dropped EF-marked SYNs. KB and runbook updates in progress.
